question: Does the Proving ground serve the pages of a seeded family of millions of pages faster than the fastest competitor on the same host consumes them (ticket #164, ADR 0064)?

proving_ground.load: 64 keep-alive HTTP/1.1 connections from one Node.js process, each asking in turn for item pages drawn uniformly from /items/1 to /items/4194304 by a seeded generator, for 10 seconds; the count is of pages answered 200
proving_ground.note: the load generator may be the bottleneck, so the figure is a lower bound of what the Proving ground serves

competitor.name: Crawlee
competitor.crawler: HttpCrawler, Crawlee's crawler that fetches without parsing, with its concurrency fixed at 64, no retries and no Session pool
competitor.urls: the same seeded draw of item URLs, given as the start list
competitor.count: pages its request handler received, over the time from run() to its end

order: alternating, the Proving ground first; each trial starts its own Proving ground
statistic: pages per second of each trial; every trial counts, none is replaced
threshold: the Proving ground's slowest trial is faster than the competitor's fastest trial
host_class: local-controlled: an unpublished run on the owner's machine (ADR 0076)

competitors_not_run.reason: not installed on this host, and installing them downloads packages, which this run does not do
